stage: Exploratory cross-target extension after the SEED-IV neural controls; no research-question adoption
inputs: All 2167 common-14 original trials; same 56 mean-window-log-bandpowers. Re-extract from waveform cache and demand exact agreement with all 1746 preceding target/source features before fitting.
folds: For each complete target participant cohort, seed-42 permutation split into five consecutive groups as evenly as possible. Rotate test group and next validation group; all remaining participants train. Every target participant tested once per initialization. No test-label stratification or fold selection.
sources: Only the original seed-42 subject split's training participants from the other two datasets; their validation/test participants are excluded
normalization: Frozen target-training-only StandardScaler for every source and held-out trial
model: Exactly the frozen SEED-IV FeatureMLP trainer: 56 -> 64 -> 32 -> 2, LayerNorm/GELU/dropout 0.2; common or three binary dataset heads; target slot zero
optimizer: AdamW 0.001, weight decay 0.01, gradient clipping 1, no scheduler/AMP/augmentation/early stopping
sampling: Batch 60, exact equal dataset quotas and equal class quotas per dataset. Independent dataset/class replacement streams, paired target draw prefixes and initial target/backbone weights
budgets: 600 updates primary; continue joint conditions to 1800 updates, giving the same 36000 available target draws as target-only. Report both; selected checkpoints may have fewer actual target exposures.
selection: Every 25 updates, target-validation trial balanced accuracy then balanced log loss. Test after both checkpoint selections. No test threshold or normalization fitted.
linear: Target-only and shared joint, same target-anchored scaler, equal dataset/class/trial weights with effective total weight fixed to target-training trial count; C 0.01/0.1/1/10 selected only on validation BA, smallest-C tie
uncertainty: All initialization results, original-trial coverage, source exclusions, participant bootstrap of pooled class-conditional counts; report class-deficient bootstrap draws rather than change cohorts. Known development tests, one fold grouping per dataset, overlapping training sets.
scope: 90 additional neural runs and 80 linear validation fits. Existing SEED-IV runs reused. No GRU/LSTM/attention comparison, native four-class learning or unseen-dataset transfer.
decision: Assess whether the observed SEED-IV pooling effect is target-dependent before proposing a contribution. All hypotheses remain exploratory; show findings and obtain explicit author approval before any adopted research-question change.
